links.outcome: Calibration intercept and slope of deployed model by race and gender
links.effect: No significant calibration difference between White and Black patients; calibration intercept significantly differed between male and female patients, underestimating malnutrition in females.
links.quote: The calibration intercept was significantly different between male and female patients.

links.outcome: Calibration drift of deployed model across years
links.effect: Both calibration intercepts and slopes statistically different between 2021 and 2022; overall intercept −1.25 (95% CI -1.28, -1.22), slope 1.55 (95% CI 1.51, 1.59).
links.quote: Both calibration intercepts and slopes were statistically different between 2021 and 2022.

links.outcome: Calibration after recalibrating the deployed model
links.effect: Recalibration improved calibration across race, gender, and year.
links.quote: Recalibration improved calibration of the model across race, gender, and year.

links.effect: Recalibration reduced miscalibration across all patient subgroups.
links.quote: Recalibration is effective at reducing miscalibration across all patient subgroups.

links.effect: Calibration intercept differed significantly between male and female patients, with underestimation in females relative to males. Calibration was not significantly different between White and Black patients; numerical subgroup estimates were not reported.
links.quote: The calibration of MUST-Plus underestimates malnutrition in females compared to males, but demonstrates similar calibration slope, suggesting similar distributions of risk estimation.

screen.practice: model recalibration and subgroup calibration monitoring
screen.reason: Evaluates a deployed machine learning model (MUST-Plus) in real-world clinical care across diverse demographics and explicitly tests recalibration as an organizational deployment practice to mitigate bias and miscalibration.
